title: Array-only DRAM wafer with periphery bonded from US 28nm logic
idea: Inverting 'cells and periphery share one wafer process': the DRAM fab builds wafers with only access devices, bitlines and capacitors (no periphery transistors, fewer implants and masks), while sense amps, decoders and I/O are made on a 28nm logic wafer in a US foundry and hybrid-bonded face-to-face at ~1 um pitch along every subarray edge.
why: Periphery (~49% of die) leaves the expensive EUV DRAM wafer, so bits per DRAM wafer rise ~1.7-1.9x, periphery moves onto depreciated US logic capacity, and sense amps get faster logic transistors.

title: One sense die multiplexed across four headless array dies
idea: Inverting 'every array owns its periphery': four stacked array dies carry only a one-transistor local preamp per bitline group, and a single logic die underneath holds the latching sense amps, decoders and I/O, selecting which die's preamps drive the shared vertical hybrid-bond column buses like a bank select along the z-axis.
why: Amortizes the ~49% periphery over four arrays so array dies are ~90% cells; stack-level cost per bit -30-40% and only one die needs logic-grade transistors.

title: Scout comparators forward speculative data before the sense amp settles
idea: Inverting 'data is valid only after the latch fully resolves': a tiny scout comparator on each selected column taps the bitlines through high-impedance gates at ~60% of tRCD and forwards data early, while the main sense amp keeps developing and restoring normally; a parity check on the scout word triggers a replay from the main latch on mismatch.
why: First-data latency -25-30% for ~1% added periphery area, because only the 64-512 selected columns get scouts; replay rate is tuned by scout timing.

title: Time-to-digital readout turns DRAM cells into two-bit cells
idea: Inverting 'a bit is one voltage compared once': after charge sharing, each bitline discharges through a cell-voltage-controlled current source and a time-to-digital converter shared by 64 columns timestamps the threshold crossing, resolving four stored charge levels per cell.
why: 2 bits per capacitor gives ~2x density without new lithography; the shared TDC adds <10% periphery. Multi-level charge margins against leakage are the hard part.

title: Coincident row-and-column select with dual-gate access transistors
idea: Inverting 'the wordline alone opens a cell': each access transistor gets a back gate tied to a column-group select line so a cell conducts only where the wordline and its column-group line are both high (like core memory's X-Y coincidence), so an activate opens 64-512 bits instead of 8 KB.
why: Cuts the 128x page overfetch toward 2-8x, lowering random-read energy ~5x from ~5.9 pJ per useful bit, and shrinks the set of rows a hammering pattern can disturb.

title: Stepwise adiabatic bitline charging from on-die tank rails
idea: Inverting 'the charge for each bitline swing is thrown away': bitlines are restored in four steps through intermediate rails held by large on-die tank capacitors, which are refilled when bitlines precharge back, so each swing dissipates about 1/N of the usual CV^2/2.
why: Bitline/array energy -50-70% for a few ns of extra restore time; attacks the CV^2 voltage-floor wall without lowering voltages.

title: Ferroelectric trim transistor nulls each sense amp's offset
idea: Inverting 'sense-amp offset is frozen at fabrication': one HZO ferroelectric trim FET in each sense amp's tail is programmed once at wafer test to cancel its measured offset, so the latch can use minimum-size transistors and resolve ~40 mV instead of ~100 mV.
why: Sense-amp area -30-40%, or alternatively ~2x less required cell charge, easing the 60-75:1 capacitor aspect-ratio wall.

title: Dithered stochastic-resonance voting for weak, leaky cells
idea: Inverting 'noise must be suppressed': during refresh and retry reads a small auxiliary comparator samples the held bitline 8 times with an injected calibrated dither and majority-votes, then forces the main latch, so cells left with only ~1/3 of nominal charge still read correctly.
why: Lets refresh intervals roughly double (refresh energy -50%, refresh is 16-33% of idle power) by tolerating deeper charge loss in the leakage tail.

title: No fuses, no spare rows: ship DRAM with a signed defect map
idea: Inverting 'every die must look perfect': delete redundant rows/columns, fuse banks and repair logic; at test, write each die's failing 4 KB pages into a signed SPD defect map and have the memory controller or OS allocator skip them like NAND bad blocks.
why: Recovers ~5-8% die area plus repair test time and raises sellable yield, for ~6-10% lower cost per bit with low technical risk; needs controller/OS support.

title: TSV-free inductive-coil stack of headless DRAM dies
idea: Inverting 'stacked dies must be wired with TSVs': thinned dies talk through top-metal coil pairs (near-field inductive links, ~1 Gb/s per coil), power arrives by edge wire bonds, and only the bottom master die carries I/O, DLL and regulators while upper dies are headless arrays.
why: Avoids the HBM TSV tax (~3x wafer area per bit vs DDR5) and its 20-30% stacking yield loss while keeping wide internal bandwidth.

title: Self-timed DRAM bank with replica-bitline completion signals
idea: Inverting 'DRAM runs on worst-case clocked timings': each mat carries a replica bitline that signals when slowest-case sensing has completed, and dual-rail sense outputs drive an asynchronous handshake to the controller, removing the DLL and fixed tRCD/tRP guard bands.
why: Typical-case accesses ~20-30% faster than worst-case specs and DLL power eliminated; attacks periphery power and latency.

title: Per-subarray micro-ring modulators replace global data lines
idea: Inverting 'data leaves the bank on copper': a silicon-nitride waveguide layer in the top BEOL runs over every subarray, each subarray's local sense output drives a micro-ring modulator on its own wavelength, and 32 subarrays share one waveguide by WDM to the package edge.
why: Replaces global I/O lines and repeaters (a large share of periphery power); targets <1 pJ/bit data movement vs 3-20 pJ/bit today.

title: Liquid-nitrogen DRAM pods with four-times-longer bitlines
idea: Inverting 'DRAM runs at room temperature': operate memory racks at 77 K, where sense-amp transistors gain ~2-3x drive with less mismatch and access-transistor leakage nearly vanishes, then redesign mats with 4x longer bitlines (fewer sense amps) and refresh effectively off.
why: Sense-amp count -50-75%, refresh energy ~0 and ~15-25% density gain from freed area; cooling overhead amortized in hyperscale pods.

title: One sense amp resolves four bitlines in sequence
idea: Inverting 'one sense amp per bitline pair': four bitline pairs charge-share simultaneously, are isolated, and hold their analog signals while a single sense amp resolves and restores them one after another in ~2 ns slots.
why: Sense-amp count -75%, freeing ~10-15% die area for a few ns of activation time; risk is signal decay and coupling during the hold.

title: Constant-weight coding with winner-take-half rank sensing
idea: Inverting 'a reference must come from a dummy cell or twin bitline': rows store data in a constant-weight code (exactly 8 ones per 16-cell group), and a winner-take-half circuit declares the 8 highest bitlines of each group to be ones, so no reference voltage exists at all.
why: Removes reference/dummy circuitry, is immune to common-mode drift and leakage, and tolerates ~2x smaller signals for robust open-bitline 4F^2 sensing, at ~15% code overhead.

title: Complementary nanotube sense amps built directly over the array
idea: Inverting 'sense amps must sit in the silicon substrate': cross-coupled sense amps are fabricated from complementary carbon-nanotube FETs at <400 C in the BEOL directly above the cell mats, pitch-matched to the bitlines through short vias.
why: Moves the largest periphery block off the substrate, shrinking the die ~20-25%; the low-temperature process does not damage capacitors below.

title: Dynamic row-well back-biasing replaces the 3 V wordline pump
idea: Inverting 'the access transistor needs a 3 V wordline': each row's access transistors sit in an isolated well that is driven with the wordline, strongly reverse-biased when off and forward-biased when selected, so a 1.2 V wordline swing gives the same on-current and off-leakage.
why: Removes VPP charge pumps (~5-8% of periphery area and notable power) and cuts wordline CV^2 ~6x; attacks the voltage floor.

title: Row decoders built from the array's own vertical transistors
idea: Inverting 'decoders are CMOS logic in the periphery': predecoded NAND-style row selection is made from series vertical-channel transistors fabricated in the same steps as the cell access devices and placed at the mat edge at cell pitch, replacing the per-mat CMOS decoder/driver stripe.
why: Shrinks the decoder/wordline-driver stripe ~50-70% (several % of die) and removes CMOS mask steps from the DRAM wafer.

title: Micro-bitlines with a gain transistor every sixteen cells
idea: Inverting 'cell charge must swing a long bitline by itself': bitlines are cut into 16-cell micro-bitlines (~3 fF) that each gate a single local gain transistor driving the global bitline, so a 1-2 fF capacitor gives a readable signal.
why: Breaks the capacitor charge wall: required Cs drops ~3x, so pillar aspect ratio can fall from ~70:1 to ~25:1, saving etch steps and yield.

title: Lazy restore: defer write-back after destructive reads
idea: Inverting 'every read must immediately restore full charge': the sense amp releases the row once cells are ~70% restored and logs the row in a small weak-row table; the refresh engine tops those rows up within their shortened retention window, or immediately if the row is re-activated.
why: tRAS -30-40%, higher bank throughput and ~15% lower row-cycle energy with little added logic.

title: Bucket-brigade row shifting replaces column decoders
idea: Inverting 'columns are picked by a decoder and mux': after sensing, the row buffer is shifted toward the I/O edge through a latch chain like a CCD image sensor, so data streams out in order without column-select lines or decoders; random columns use 16-position skip taps.
why: Removes column decoders and CSL wiring (~8-12% of periphery) and suits streaming AI tensor reads, at some random-access latency cost.

title: Open array-to-periphery bond standard for merchant cell wafers
idea: Inverting 'one company makes the whole DRAM die': publish an open hybrid-bond interface (bitline pitch, preamp spec, power and test pads) so array fabs sell bare cell wafers and many periphery designers, including US logic foundries, sell sense/decode dies, like UCIe for memory internals.
why: Splits the $15B integrated fab into an array-only fab plus commodity logic, lowering capital intensity and entry barriers; the US can take periphery share immediately.

title: Leaky charge-packet activation counter cell in every row
idea: Inverting 'row-hammer tracking needs digital counters': each row gets one extra cell in a counter column that receives a fixed charge packet on every activation instead of being restored; the same sense amp compares it to a threshold during activate, refreshing neighbors and resetting it when crossed, while natural leakage forgets old activations like a sliding window.
why: Replaces multi-bit per-row counters and read-modify-write (as in activation-counting schemes) with one cell per row, closing ~1k-activation hammer exposure at <0.1% area.

title: Each cell is its own sense amp: stacked oxide latches
idea: Inverting 'storage and amplification are separate': each bit is a 4-transistor cross-coupled latch of n-IGZO and p-SnO thin-film transistors stacked in 8 BEOL tiers, so the cell itself drives the bitline rail-to-rail and per-bitline sense amps shrink to one shared buffer per 256 columns.
why: Deletes sense-amp stripes (~20% of die) and refresh entirely, with tiers recovering density; oxide leakage keeps static power tiny. No capacitor anywhere.

title: Thyristor columns where an inverter replaces the sense amp
idea: Inverting 'the cell signal is millivolts': vertical npnp thyristor cells latch on with ~10-30 uA read current versus pA off, so bitlines swing to the rail within ns and each column is read by a skewed inverter with a keeper; reads are nondestructive, so the restore phase disappears.
why: Periphery ~30% smaller (no latch sense amp, no half-VDD precharge, no restore) and tRC ~5 ns, with no capacitor to scale.

title: Self-restoring floating-body read deletes the write-back path
idea: Inverting 'a read disturbs the cell and needs restore circuitry': floating-body cells are read with drain bias just into impact ionization, so a '1' cell regenerates its own body holes through bipolar gain while a '0' cell stays empty, making every read a self-refresh.
why: Removes write-back drivers and restore timing from the column periphery, cuts read energy ~30%, and makes hot rows refresh themselves.

title: Twin-FeFET race: first-to-conduct wins, no reference needed
idea: Inverting 'sensing compares a cell against a reference': each bit is stored as opposite polarizations in two FeFETs; their shared gate is ramped and a tiny arbiter latches whichever drain current crosses first, so the decision needs no reference voltage and the read is nondestructive.
why: Eliminates reference generators and restore, rejects common-mode Vt drift and temperature, and drops read energy to the arbiter's few fJ; 2 cells/bit offset by vertical 4F^2 FeFETs.

title: Bistable buckled-nanobeam cell read by a single pull-up
idea: Inverting 'the bit is an electrical state': each bit is the up/down position of a buckled nanobeam that touches a contact only when down; reading is an ohmic open-or-short, so a weak pull-up and an inverter replace the sense amp, with zero leakage and no refresh.
why: Near-infinite on/off ratio removes sense-margin problems and all refresh energy; periphery becomes trivial. Contact wear and stiction limit endurance (~1e10-1e12).

title: Phase-encoded parametron cells read by frequency multiplexing
idea: Inverting 'every bit needs its own wire to a sense amp': bits are the 0 or pi phase of parametrically pumped nanomechanical resonators, each tuned to a distinct frequency, so one shared readout line and one phase-detecting receiver demodulate 32 cells at once.
why: Sense-amp count drops ~32x and the pump keeps each bit alive continuously instead of by refresh; attacks periphery area and leakage, but is speculative on density.

title: Move the bits, not the sensor: one read head per track
idea: Inverting 'every bit sits still and sensing comes to it': 64 bits are stored as magnetic domains along a vertical nanowire and shifted by current pulses past a single MTJ read head at the track base, so one sense amp and one access device serve 64 bits.
why: Sense-amp and access-device count drop ~64x, magnetic state has unlimited endurance and no refresh; shift latency of ~10-30 ns keeps it DRAM-class for row-buffered access.

title: Spin-to-charge sign readout instead of measuring resistance
idea: Inverting 'magnetic bits are read by their resistance magnitude': a small supply current through each nanomagnet into a heavy-metal/oxide interface produces an inverse Rashba-Edelstein voltage whose sign follows the magnetization, and that signed voltage directly drives the gate of a single sense transistor.
why: Sign detection needs no reference and no TMR margin, so the sense amp collapses to one transistor and read disturb vanishes; capacitor-free.

title: Vanadium-dioxide hysteretic latch held inside its Mott window
idea: Inverting 'volatile memory must leak and be refreshed': each cell is a tiny VO2 element biased inside its metal-insulator hysteresis window, so it stays metallic or insulating as long as the hold bias is on, and a current comparator reads the ~100x resistance ratio.
why: One-element static cell with no refresh controller, no capacitor and a large read signal; hold power and thermal crosstalk are the risks.

title: Esaki tunnel-diode Goto pair as a static one-transistor cell
idea: Inverting 'a DRAM cell stores charge': two series interband tunnel diodes form a bistable node via negative differential resistance, gated onto the bitline by one access transistor, and the node already sits at one of two latched levels so the column needs only a simple comparator.
why: Static storage with no refresh and no capacitor at ~1T area, with nA hold current; diode peak-current uniformity at scale is the risk.

title: Conductive ferroelectric domain walls give nondestructive reads
idea: Inverting 'ferroelectric reads are destructive': in thin-film lithium niobate cells, switching creates a conducting domain wall between electrodes, so the state is read as a 1e3-1e5 current ratio without switching the polarization.
why: Nondestructive, high-margin reads remove restore circuitry and refresh; uses a non-tungsten, non-EUV material stack; endurance of wall motion (~1e10+) must be proven.

title: Superconducting nanowire-loop memory with single-flux-quantum sensing
idea: Inverting 'memory sensing is analog voltage at room temperature': bits are clockwise or counter-clockwise persistent currents in kinetic-inductance nanowire loops at 4 K, read by a single-flux-quantum comparator that switches only for one current direction, for cryogenic AI and quantum-control racks.
why: Read energy ~1e-18 J with no leakage and no refresh; periphery in SFQ logic. Density and cooling cost make it speculative.

title: Low-barrier volatile MRAM refreshed by stock DRAM periphery
idea: Inverting 'MRAM must be nonvolatile': thin free layers with an energy barrier of ~20-30 kT keep data for ms to seconds and switch with ~10x less current, and the existing DRAM refresh controller periodically re-writes them while TMR sensing reads them.
why: Unlimited magnetic endurance with fJ-class writes and tiny cells, reusing DRAM's refresh and timing periphery unchanged; no capacitor.

title: Complementary MTJ voltage divider readable by an inverter
idea: Inverting 'MRAM needs a sensitive sense amp': each bit is two MTJs written to opposite states and stacked as a voltage divider, so the mid-node swings ~0.3 V between states and a plain skewed inverter at the column replaces the current-mode sense amp.
why: Removes reference cells and analog sense amps, cutting column periphery ~25% and read latency to a few ns; capacitor-free.

title: Compressed-sensing reads via random multi-row current sums
idea: Inverting 'each bit is sensed individually': in capacitorless FeFET NOR columns, 16 random-pattern wordline combinations are activated and the summed bitline currents go to a 4-bit ADC, from which sparse 64-cell groups (mostly zeros, as in activations and zero pages) are reconstructed.
why: Up to ~4x fewer sense operations and less I/O energy for sparse data; dense groups fall back to normal reads.

title: Universal programmable sense front-end die for any capacitorless array
idea: Inverting 'periphery is designed for one cell type': a merchant logic die with sense channels configurable in current, voltage, or time mode is hybrid-bonded to any capacitorless array (thyristor, FeFET, floating-body, MTJ), so new cell startups only build arrays.
why: Removes ~2-3 years and most periphery design cost from each new memory technology and gives a volume product for US logic fabs.

title: US periphery foundry-as-a-service for capacitorless memory startups
idea: Inverting 'each memory maker owns its fab end to end': a CHIPS-funded shared 28nm line runs standard sense/decode wafers and bonding for any capacitorless cell startup, paid per wafer, with guaranteed government purchase of first products.
why: Cuts a startup's capital need from $15B+ to array-only lines, builds US manufacturability and diversifies away from three incumbent DRAM makers.

title: Threshold-graded tier select replaces staircase contacts in 3D
idea: Inverting 'each tier of a 3D stack needs its own staircase contact and driver': each tier's select transistor in a stacked capacitorless (floating-body or thyristor) array is given a different threshold voltage by graded work-function gates, so one shared vertical gate line picks the tier by voltage level.
why: Removes staircase etch and per-tier drivers, a major area and process cost of 26+ tier 3D DRAM; breaks the 3D break-even barrier sooner.

title: Photovoltaic wordline drivers fed by waveguide light
idea: Inverting 'wordlines are driven by metal and charge pumps': a BEOL waveguide carries light to series photodiode stacks at each floating-body row segment, generating the gate voltage locally when a row's micro-ring is tuned on, so no high-voltage wordline drivers or pumps exist.
why: Eliminates charge pumps and HV driver stripes and isolates rows electrically (helps disturb); speculative on speed and optical power.

title: Surface acoustic wave pulses select rows of magnetostrictive bits
idea: Inverting 'rows are selected by wires carrying current': a SAW transducer launches a strain pulse timed to reach the target row of magnetostrictive nanomagnets, lowering their barrier so a weak shared field line writes only that row, while reads use local MTJs.
why: Replaces high-current write drivers and per-row write selectors with timing; write energy ~10x lower; speculative.

title: Three-terminal SOT cells give read-while-write banks
idea: Inverting 'reads and writes share one path': spin-orbit-torque cells have separate write (heavy-metal line) and read (MTJ) terminals, so each bank gets an independent read sense path and write driver and can serve a read and a write in the same cycle.
why: Removes write-to-read turnaround and bank conflicts, raising effective bandwidth ~20-40% without more banks; capacitor-free with unlimited endurance.

title: Mixed mat: fast floating-body and nonvolatile FeFET share sense amps
idea: Inverting 'one array holds one cell type': alternate rows in a mat are floating-body (fast, volatile) and FeFET (nonvolatile), both read by drain current, and one dual-mode current sense amp switches bias between them so hot data and persistent data live in the same mat.
why: Gives a hot tier and a no-refresh tier for the cost of one periphery, cutting refresh power for cold data ~90%.

title: Leakage-balanced bistable floating body that needs no refresh controller
idea: Inverting 'leakage is the enemy': floating-body cells are biased so gate-induced drain leakage generation and junction recombination balance at two stable body potentials, so each cell holds its state statically and the refresh counter, scheduler and temperature-based refresh logic are deleted.
why: Removes refresh energy (~46 fJ/bit, 16-33% idle power) and its 10-20% bandwidth tax plus refresh periphery; capacitor-free.
